title: Britain Planned a 2,000-Foot Aircraft Carrier Made of Ice

scenes.text: In World War Two, Britain planned an aircraft carrier made of ice.
The idea was pykrete, which is frozen water mixed with wood pulp or sawdust.
It was far tougher than normal ice and resisted bullets.
The plan was a ship two thousand feet long with walls forty feet thick.
A sixty-foot test model was built in the Canadian Rockies.
But the cost exploded, and it was cancelled. The ice ship never sailed.

description:
Britain planned Project Habakkuk, an aircraft carrier about two thousand feet long with forty-foot-thick walls made of pykrete, frozen water and wood pulp.
A sixty-foot test model was built in Canada before it was cancelled in 1944.
Would you have sailed on it?
first_comment: The prototype was built on Patricia Lake in Alberta in 1943. What other wild wartime idea should we cover?
